# rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_type (Resource)

Manages a direct Iris agent-memory resource, independently of Redis Cloud CAPI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_type" "example" {
  store_id    = rediscloud_iris_agent_memory.example.id
  name        = "preferences"
  description = "User preferences"
  fields_json = jsonencode([{
    name        = "topic"
    description = "Preference topic"
    type        = "STRING"
  }])
  extraction_strategy_json = jsonencode({
    prompt  = "Extract the user's preferences."
    enabled = true
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Human-readable description of what this memory type captures.
- `name` (String) Unique type name within the store. Must not collide with built-in types
(semantic, episodic, message, session_summary, session_summary_view).
- `store_id` (String) Server-generated store identifier: st_ followed by 32 lowercase hex characters.

### Optional

- `extraction_strategy_json` (String) JSON-encoded service configuration. Use jsonencode(...). Extraction strategy for a custom memory type.
- `fields_json` (String) JSON-encoded service configuration. Use jsonencode(...). Structured fields that make up a record of this type. Optional; a type with no
fields accepts direct writes carrying no structured attributes.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier used for import.
- `revision` (String) Opaque revision returned on reads. Server assigned; ignored on creation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import rediscloud_iris_agent_memory_type.example st_11111111111111111111111111111111/preferences
```
